summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch, implement identified fixes, and get the PR merged to main — including resolving all CI failures and reviewer comments.
summary.outcome: All high/medium security findings were fixed and verified, the PR was merged to main, a post-merge desktop E2E regression was diagnosed and fixed (sequence number mismatch in parseCachedRecord + unseeded PublishCoordinator cache), and a follow-up PR #449 was created for the regression fix.

repo: IPNS names are cryptographically derived from Ed25519 public keys via deriveIpnsName() — client-side verification must bind pubKey to ipnsName to prevent key substitution attacks
The @cipherbox/crypto package has ESM-only transitive dependencies (@libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, multiformats) that break NestJS (CJS) unless bundled with noExternal in tsup CJS config
tsup must use separate CJS and ESM build configs — noExternal on CJS only; ESM must keep deps external for Vite/Rollup browser builds

The desktop FUSE client's PublishCoordinator initializes with an empty seq_cache and never seeds from the pre-populate IPNS resolve at mount, causing first-write conflicts if resolve_sequence returns stale data

upsertFolderIpns always increments the DB sequenceNumber by 1 regardless of what sequence is embedded in the published record bytes — parseCachedRecord must use cached.sequenceNumber (the DB column) as authoritative, not the sequence parsed from signedRecord bytes
The Verify API Spec CI job needs @cipherbox/crypto built before pnpm api:generate because the NestJS bootstrap imports it

Desktop vault init: the Rust client publishes root folder IPNS at sequence 0 (record bytes), but upsertFolderIpns stores sequence 1 in the DB — this discrepancy was masked before parseCachedRecord was introduced

The desktop E2E test passes --secret as TEST_SECRET env var (not CLI arg) after the security fix — CI uses TEST_LOGIN_SECRET which maps to TEST_SECRET in the shell script via ${TEST_SECRET:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}

code.finding: pubKey-to-ipnsName binding check: after verifying Ed25519 signature, derive expected IPNS name from returned pubKey bytes and compare to requested ipnsName
Replaced spread-operator base64 (stack overflow risk on large records) with String.fromCharCode loop + btoa; also added publicKey derivation and forwarding on publish
Server-side pubKey-to-ipnsName validation: if dto.publicKey provided, derive IPNS name from it and reject if it doesn't match dto.ipnsName

parseCachedRecord must use cached.sequenceNumber (DB column) as the returned sequenceNumber, not the sequence embedded in the signedRecord bytes — the DB column is always incremented by upsertFolderIpns and is authoritative
Equal-sequence cache enrichment: when networkSeq === dbSeq, merge cached signatureV2/data/pubKey into network result before returning so signature verification works for network-resolved records
MaxLength(100) for publicKey field — base64-encoded 32-byte Ed25519 key is 44 chars; 100 gives headroom without allowing arbitrary large strings
PublishCoordinator must be seeded with sequence numbers from pre-populate IPNS resolves at mount time; added record_publish calls for root and subfolder sequences
Split into two defineConfig entries: CJS with noExternal: [/.*/ ] (fully self-contained bundle), ESM with default externals (Vite-compatible)

workflow: 1Password SSH agent intermittently fails to sign commits — retrying usually works after a few seconds

When ESM-only deps are in the dependency tree of a package consumed by both NestJS (CJS) and Vite (ESM), the package needs split tsup configs rather than a single noExternal that breaks browser builds
Desktop E2E only runs on main push, not PR branches — regressions from merged code are only caught post-merge
Before reproducing locally, simulate the API flow with curl to quickly verify sequence/state assumptions rather than building the full desktop binary
upload-artifact@v7 on Windows cannot upload files outside the repo root (e.g. runner.temp) without explicit root-directory configuration

friction: 1Password SSH agent repeatedly failed to sign git commits, requiring multiple retry attempts throughout the session
noExternal: [/.*/ ] on tsup broke the desktop Vite build — required a second iteration to discover the CJS/ESM split config approach
The @cipherbox/crypto CJS bundle was missing index.d.ts because the ESM config with clean: true was wiping the CJS output — required careful build ordering
Desktop E2E only runs on main, so the sequence number regression was only discovered post-merge, requiring a separate hotfix PR
The Verify API Spec CI job didn't build @cipherbox/crypto first, causing it to fail — required an additional CI workflow fix commit
Main branch is protected — the post-merge regression fix required creating a new branch and PR rather than pushing directly
